messages:
oncall-bot: [ALERT] region=fra1 control-plane heartbeat missing > 90% nodes. Errors: API 503 / scheduler timeouts. Severity: P1. https://monitoring.redwood.internal/alerts/ALR-7632

maria: seeing the same on dashboards — GPU pod evictions + controlplane reconciler errors. Console shows many nodes NotReady.

asha: I’m oncall and taking IC. Quick check: is this fabric/network or cloud provider issue?

kevin: I see a spike in inter-pod network latency and BGP withdraws for fra1 spine switches in the metrics. Routing instability looks likely.

kai: looking at provider status: API returns 500s for some endpoints. Could be provider-side network partition.

infra-bot: Cloud provider maintenance event detected for fra1: maintenance_id=mn-2026-045, state=investigating. Provider ticket: https://cloud.provider/status/incident/98765

maria: declare incident page, assign ops runbook FRA-OUTAGE-1. Asha — you’re IC, Kevin SRE lead. Tom infra lead.

asha: acknowledged. Creating incident doc and inviting relevant folks. Support — please prepare customer comms for any Dedicated customers pinned to fra1.

support-bot: Draft created in /incidents/fra1-outage/draft-comm.md. Tagging sales-eng for priority customers.

sales-eng: alerted. List of impacted Dedicated tenants attached to the comms doc.

kevin: immediate mitigation plan: 1) start traffic shift for non-sensitive routes away from fra1 2) scale up capacity in lon1/ams1 for GPU workloads 3) enable automatic model-fallback on affected routes. I’ll kick off step 1 now.

tom: provisioning: lon1 has reserved capacity but we’ll need to evict lower-priority jobs. I’m running reservation rebalancer to free GPUs.

maria: set routing policy to prefer lon1/ams1 and reduce fra1 weight to 0 for public API. Keep dedicated customer routing pinned until we have data.

kevin: running traffic shift command:
```
# run from routing-control
routectl set-weight --region fra1 0 --regions lon1=0.6,ams1=0.4 --policy gradual --canary 10
```

asha: monitoring canary for errors and latency. If anything spikes, pause and rollback.

kai: network logs show heartbeats from control-plane VMs dropped simultaneously ~2163009965. Correlates with provider event start time.

infra-bot: provider API also shows inter-region packet loss between fra1 and backbone ~20%.

maria: action items: oncall -> keep traffic shift running and monitor, tom -> speed up reservation rebalance and confirm GPU availability, kevin -> verify canary and escalate to routing-engineer if packet loss follows traffic shift.

kevin: canary at 10% looks good so far (latency +3ms, error rate flat). advancing to 50%.

tom: freed 60 GPUs in lon1 by evicting batch jobs. Starting targeted reschedules for real-time services.

asha: support — send status update to affected customers: basic note about increased latencies and active mitigation; we will avoid automated failover for pinned Dedicated tenants without ops signoff.

support-bot: update sent to customers on the list.

maria: short term - enable model-quantization fallback on high-cost routes to lower GPU footprint until we stabilize. This reduces compute needs and helps capacity. Kevin can coordinate which routes.

kevin: enabling fallback for public-generation routes now. Command: `service-config update --route gen-* --fallback quantized-v2`

kai: provider says they are investigating spine switch control-plane reloads. No ETA yet.

asha: escalate to provider support with ticket mn-2026-045 and ask for network engineer bridge. Assigning provider escalation owner: tom.

tom: escalation opened, bridging with provider; sharing bridge link in doc.

maria: operations note — this will increase cross-region egress and GPU spot usage; finance heads up: we’ll exceed normal burn for the next 24h.

sales-eng: flagged high-value tenants that might require dedicated manual failover to lon1.

asha: next steps: 1) maintain traffic shift to avoid fra1 2) confirm GPU capacity in lon1/ams1 3) keep customers updated 4) provider escalation and ETA. I’ll run a status check every 15 min.

oncall-bot: Incident declared: FRA1_NETWORK_PARTITION. Incident channel: #inc-fra1-outage. Current severity: P1. IC=asha, SRE lead=kevin, Infra lead=tom.

maria: thanks team — keep updates concise. Post next update in 10m with canary results and provider ETA if available. :thumbsup:
